title: NLTI Overview (pos-mcp-server)
description: Request health for the NL-interface. Counters/timers come from Prometheus (pos-mcp-server /actuator/prometheus). True latency percentiles and per-outcome splits come from the nlti.request.telemetry log stream in Loki. See https://github.com/louisburroughs/durion/blob/master/domains/general/mcp-server/operations/dashboards/nlti-overview.md.

panels.title: NLTI request count (per min)
panels.description: nlt.request.count is an untagged Micrometer counter incremented once per NltiRequestService.submit(). It carries no status/route tags, so the per-route split lives in the panel to the right.

panels.title: HTTP requests by route and status (per min)
panels.description: The route/status split the untagged nlt.request.count cannot give. uri is the Spring templated path, so /v1/nlt/requests/{requestId}/confirm stays one series.

panels.title: Chat outcome mix (telemetry)
panels.description: outcome.status / outcome.errorCode from nlti.request.telemetry. Covers the /v1/mcp/chat and /chat/stream paths, which do not increment nlt.request.count.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome_status) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Chat end-to-end latency p50/p95/p99 (telemetry)
panels.description: True percentiles, computed in Loki over latency.totalMs from nlti.request.telemetry. Prometheus cannot supply these: pos-mcp-server does not import application-observability.yml, so no percentile histograms are published for any timer.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.50, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | unwrap latency_totalMs [$__interval])

quantile_over_time(0.95, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | unwrap latency_totalMs [$__interval])

quantile_over_time(0.99, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | unwrap latency_totalMs [$__interval])

panels.title: /v1/nlt/requests submit latency (mean)
panels.description: Micrometer timer nlt.request.latency_ms (the one NltiRequestServiceImpl actually records; the nlt.request.latency bean in NltiObservabilityMetricsConfig is registered but never sampled). Mean only — no histogram buckets are published.

panels.title: NLTI planning latency (mean)
panels.description: GAP: nlt.planning.latency is registered as a bean in NltiObservabilityMetricsConfig but no code path records a sample, so the series exists with count 0. Panel is correct and will populate once the planning stage is timed.

panels.title: NLTI execution latency (mean)
panels.description: GAP: nlt.execution.latency, mcp.model.latency and mcp.tool.execution.latency are all registered-but-never-recorded timers. Same caveat as the planning panel.

panels.title: NLTI errors by error code (telemetry)
panels.description: nlt.error.count is untagged; the per-code breakdown comes from outcome.errorCode in the telemetry stream.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome_errorCode) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | outcome_status = "ERROR" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Audit write failures (1h)
panels.description: nlt.audit.write_failures is incremented by AuditLedgerServiceImpl whenever the append-only ledger write throws. Any non-zero value is a P1: destructive events re-throw and block execution.

panels.title: Intent parses and clarifications (per min)
panels.description: nlt.intent.parse.count fires once per IntentParserService.parse(); nlt.intent.clarification.count fires when the parse could not resolve an intent. A rising clarification ratio is the primary intent-regression signal.

panels.title: Tagging latency p50/p95 (telemetry)
panels.description: tagging.latencyMs from nlti.request.telemetry (schemaVersion 3): the wall time of the provider call, over every turn that called the provider (mode SHADOW or ENFORCE), fallbacks included. The tagging block is also present in mode OFF (the heuristic tagger always runs) but carries no latencyMs there; OFF turns are filtered out. The per-call budget is mcp.tagging.provider.timeout (800 ms); a p95 near it means many turns are paying the timeout. The bake-off p50/p95 over answered turns only comes from scripts/tagging_shadow_report.py.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | drop telemetry | json tagging_mode="tagging.mode", tagging_latencyMs="tagging.latencyMs" | __error__="" | tagging_mode != "" | tagging_mode != "OFF" | tagging_latencyMs != "" | unwrap tagging_latencyMs [$__interval]) by (service)

quantile_over_time(0.95, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | drop telemetry | json tagging_mode="tagging.mode", tagging_latencyMs="tagging.latencyMs" | __error__="" | tagging_mode != "" | tagging_mode != "OFF" | tagging_latencyMs != "" | unwrap tagging_latencyMs [$__interval]) by (service)

panels.title: Tagging fallbacks by reason (telemetry)
panels.description: Turns per tagging.fallbackReason (timeout, rate_limited, error, malformed: the provider failed), over tagged turns in mode SHADOW or ENFORCE. The tagging block is also present in mode OFF (heuristic only, no provider call) and those turns are excluded everywhere here. Series 'provider failure share' is what the NltiTaggingFallbackRateHigh alert (P2) fires on above 20% for 15m. Wave 1 sets no turn-level low_confidence reason (low confidence is per tag, in enforce), so there is no low-confidence share series or alert yet; that signal is deferred to Wave 2. The per-tag threshold view is scripts/tagging_shadow_report.py.

targets.expr: sum by (tagging_fallbackReason) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | drop telemetry | json tagging_mode="tagging.mode", tagging_fallbackReason="tagging.fallbackReason" | __error__="" | tagging_mode != "" | tagging_mode != "OFF" | tagging_fallbackReason != "" [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | drop telemetry | json tagging_mode="tagging.mode", tagging_fallbackReason="tagging.fallbackReason" | __error__="" | tagging_mode != "" | tagging_mode != "OFF" | tagging_fallbackReason=~"timeout|rate_limited|error|malformed" [$__interval])) / sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | drop telemetry | json tagging_mode="tagging.mode" | __error__="" | tagging_mode != "" | tagging_mode != "OFF" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Tagger agreement rate (telemetry)
panels.description: Mean of tagging.agreementRate: the share of tags per turn where the model and the heuristic agree, present only when both answered (never in mode OFF). Use scripts/tagging_shadow_report.py for the per-tag and per-threshold breakdown that sets mcp.tagging.thresholds.<tag>.

targets.expr: avg_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | drop telemetry | json tagging_mode="tagging.mode", tagging_agreementRate="tagging.agreementRate" | __error__="" | tagging_mode != "" | tagging_mode != "OFF" | tagging_agreementRate != "" | unwrap tagging_agreementRate [$__interval]) by (service)

panels.title: Tagging provider model in use (telemetry)
panels.description: Turns per tagging.providerModel over the dashboard range (providerModel is present only when the provider was called, so mode OFF turns never appear). More than one row means the model changed inside the window (a bake-off, or a config roll).

targets.expr: sum by (tagging_providerModel) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | drop telemetry | json tagging_providerModel="tagging.providerModel" | __error__="" | tagging_providerModel != "" [$__range]))

panels.title: ollama container memory (cAdvisor)
panels.description: Working-set memory of the ollama container (cAdvisor container_memory_working_set_bytes), which serves the embedding model (bge-m3) and the tagging model side by side. ADR-0068 section 6 measures each bake-off candidate's resident memory here: read the value with both models warm (after a gate batch, `ollama ps` listing both), minus the embedding-only baseline. The model's resident memory belongs in the cell's memory budget (ADR-0068 Implementation Notes, Container).

panels.title: ollama container CPU (cAdvisor)
panels.description: CPU used by the ollama container, in cores (cAdvisor container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, 5m rate). On the GPU-less host every tagging call and every embedding runs on these cores, so a sustained plateau near the host's core count explains rising tagging latency and timeouts.

panels.title: Raw nlti.request.telemetry stream
panels.description: Drill-down for any spike window. Each line is one JSON telemetry event; correlationId links to the audit ledger (/v1/nlt/audit) and to scripts/nlti_live_verify.py evidence.
